valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2028E diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date in November 2027, anchored to FY2026 actual diluted EPS of $2.10 and FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $1.15-$1.35)

bear.driver: Prolonged Greater China (-26% ex-FX in Q1 FY27) and Sportswear/Jordan resets with slower Pace cost-savings realization

base.driver: High-single-digit FY27 revenue decline stabilizes in FY28 as North America performance growth offsets China/classic resets and Pace savings lift margins

bull.driver: Faster North America and global performance running/football momentum, cleaner wholesale/digital inventory, and Pace savings ahead of plan

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2028E EPS of $1.65, the $37.99 close implies 23.0x (above the 21x base multiple, or $1.81 EPS at 21x); the $30.71 simple-average named-analyst target implies 18.6x base EPS or $1.46 EPS at 21x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $1.65 (4.3 pp of price return).
valuation.watch_metric: Greater China currency-neutral revenue growth and NIKE Brand gross margin progression (42.8% in Q1 FY27)

analyst_notes: Following NIKE's Q1 FY2027 earnings release and FY2027 guidance reset on October 1, 2026, all seven named analysts cut targets or downgraded, with targets clustered between $24 and $39 (simple average $30.71, -19.2% vs. the $37.99 close, compared with -8.8% for the $34.65 base case). The ~10.4 pp gap reflects Street skepticism on the pace of Greater China and Sportswear recovery—Truist downgraded to Sell at $29 on November 5, and BofA ($24) and Morgan Stanley ($27) sit near our bear case. Note that post-cutoff Investor Day updates (November 16-17, 2026) are excluded per the November 13, 2026 cutoff.
